scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Arithmetic Stein-degree bounds for log Calabi–Yau pairs” (preprints/Arithmetic-Stein-degree-bounds-for-log-Calabi-Yau-pairs-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 034 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 41101b5f371f3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every integer 𝑑 ≥ 1 and real number 𝑡 > 0, there is an integer 𝑁(𝑑, 𝑡) ≥ 1 with the following property. Let 𝑘 be any field of characteristic zero, and let (𝑋, 𝐵) be a projective log canonical Q-pair such that dim 𝑋 = 𝑑, 𝐻0 (𝑋, O𝑋) = 𝑘, 𝐾𝑋 + 𝐵 ∼Q 0. Assume that 𝑋 is normal and integral and that 𝐵 is effective. If 𝑆 is a prime component of 𝐵 with coefficient at least 𝑡, then 𝑐(𝑆/𝑘) ≤ 𝑁(𝑑, 𝑡). Consequently sdeg(𝑆/Spec 𝑘) ≤ dim𝑘 𝐻0 (𝑆𝜈 , O𝑆𝜈 ) = 𝑐(𝑆/𝑘) ≤ 𝑁(𝑑, 𝑡), where 𝑆𝜈 is the normalization of 𝑆.
